newsitem.title: GERMANY: Novartis Pharma Gmbh eyes stronger growth.
newsitem.headline: Novartis Pharma Gmbh eyes stronger growth.

text.p: Novartis Pharma GmbH, the German drugs unit of Swiss health care giant Novartis AG, said on Thursday that it plans to grow more strongly than the broad market even though 1997 sales have so far been unsatisfying.

Silvio Gabriel, the pharmaceutical group's head, said sales at the unit stood at around 1.2 billion marks ($700.2 million) in 1996. Novartis AG, the parent company, posted 1996 sales of 36.2 billion Swiss francs ($24.4 billion).
Gabriel also said the German unit plans further job cuts, paring the workforce back to 1,550 by 1999 from 1,800 last year when Novartis was created after Swiss Ciba-Geigy AG merged with Sandoz AG.

In the first two months of this year, however, Gabriel described turnover as "unsatisfactory", explaining that German health laws had created uncertainty among physicians prompting them to scale back prescriptions of various drugs.

Under German law physicians are given a so-called health care budget which allots them a sum of money for prescriptions. The German pharmaceutical industry has said that physicians often try to prescribe cheaper generic drugs in order to stay within their budget limits.
Earlier this year Gabriel said Novartis' ongoing strong drugs research should allow the group to launch two to three new products annually.

Novartis Deutschland, which includes the drugs group consumer health and Ciba Visison, is currently Germany's number one life sciences group (pharmaceuticals, generics, consumer care), edging past Hoechst Marion Roussel last year.
